full_judgment:
2. The petitioner Mrs. Alam Ara Huq is the wife of the detenu Ansarul Huq who was Ex-Manager, Agrani Bank, Khatunganj Branch, Chittagong. Upon an ELR. lodged by the Inspector of Police, Anti-Corruption Department, Kotwali P.S. Case No. 12 dated 16.7.86 under sections 420/409/ 467/468/471/447/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1947 was started against the detenu and others for alleged misappropriation of Taka 4 crores of Agrani Bank. On 11.7.86 the detenu was arrested by the police from the Agrani Bank, Laldighi Branch, Chittagong and was remanded to custody. In Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.921 of 1986 the learned Sessions Judge, Chittagong granted bail to the detenu on 24.12.86 on the ground that no charge could be established against the detenu during investigation. Another criminal case, namely Kotwali P.S. Case No.46(l2) of 1986 for similar offence was started against the detenu, but in that case also the detenu was enlarged on bail by the learned Sessions Judge, Chittagong. The detenu was suspended from service with effect from 12.7.86. Since then he resided at Dhaka and he never misused the privilege of bail in the criminal case against him. He has been attending Chittagong Court on every date without any latches. 

 4. On 29.8.88 the police submitted charge sheet against the detenu and 8 others in D.A.B.G.R. case No. 26 of 1986 arising out of Kotwali P.S. Case , No. 12(7)/86 under sections 120B/420/409/467/468/471/477A/109/34 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1947. 

 "Ground No.1 being the subject matter of an independent criminal prosecution could have been taken as a ground of the impugned order of detention and on this ground the detente, of the detenu is unlawful and without lawful authority. The ground Nos. 2, 3, 4 and 5 show that there are no specific and definite allegations, therein and these are vague and "are in general, terms. As such, all these four grounds suffer from vagueness. It is also a settled principle that even if one of the several grounds of detention is found to be vague the whole order of detention falls through, because, in case of vagueness even of a single ground the detenu is deprive. His statutory right to file an effective representation. As it appears that in the present case, four grounds i. e. the ground Nos. 2-5 are vague, we are of the opinion that these vague gounds have rendered the entire order of detention illegal and unlawful." 

 16. It has been held in the case of Abdul Latif Mirza Vs. Government of Bangladesh and others, 31 DLR(AD) 1, that even an independent order of the Government purporting to continue an earlier detention will be illegal if the detenu continued in detention without any order whatsoever and if the subsequent order of detention is passed and served after the expiry of the initial order of detention. 

 17. The present case is not one of expiry of the original order of detention. It is a case of both the first and second orders of detention being declared illegal by two orders of this Court. As soon as the illegality of the order of detention is communicated to the respondents, the order of detention loses its force and becomes an illegal order, unless appealed against and also a stay is obtained from the Appellate Division. If the detenu is not released on receipt of the order of this Court and if he is continued in detention without any order whatsoever, then his detention becomes an illegal detention. By serving a fresh order of detention after two days on 11.3.89 the Government merely continued an illegal detention. The order dated 11.3.89 is no doubt an independent order but is a still-born detention order and it continues as such. As the Appellate Division has stated, there is no co-relation between an independent order and the fact of independent detention. The order of detention purporting to continue an illegal detention cannot be sustained. The third order of detention falls through on this ground alone. 

 24. We find that the fourth and last order of detention dated 8.7.89 was passed in confirmation of the Ministry's order of detention dated 11.3.89. It is Our finding that the order of detention dated 11.3.89 is illegal. The latest order in confirmation of an illegal order of detention is so patently illegal. Further, it has been stated in the last detention order  (Annexure N) that it has been passed under section 3 (3) of the special Power Act, 1974. An order of detention under section 3(3) of the Special Power Act is passed by the Government in approval of an order of detention passed by the District Magistrate or an Additional District Magistrate. In the present case no order of detention was passed by any District Magistrate or any Additional District Magistrate detaining the detenu. This only shows that the detaining authority has not applied its mind to the facts and circumstances of the case and has acted mindlessly, nervously and desperately to keep the detenu in detention somehow. 

 25. Anticipating the possible defence that the fourth order of detention dated 8.7.89 has not been specifically challenged in this writ petition, Mr. Chowdhury has relied upon the case of Mrs. Sajeda Parvin Banu Vs. Government of Bangladesh and others, BCR 1988 (AD) 89, in which the Appellate Division has held that in issuing a Rule Nisi in a habeas corpus writ petition it is the detention of the detenu itself against which relief is sought. It is not the question of order of detention. The constitutional power vested by the Constitution in the High Court Division cannot be limited or taken away by a sub-constitutional legislation. 

 27. As we have stated before, the detenu was ordered to be released by this Court on as many as two occasions in the past. The advance order of release was served on the respondents. Those orders were defied. Fresh orders of detention were served upon the detenu in jail on both the occasions without complying with the orders of this Court. We have directed the corpus of the detenu to be brought before us today in view of this exceptional situation in order to ensure that our order is carried out if we decide to release the detenu. We do hereby declare that the detenu Ansarul Huq has been detained without lawful authority and is being held in custody without lawful authority and in an unlawful manner. We direct his immediate release from this Court premises if not wanted in connection with any other case.
